of: A mechanism by which a previously available course of action becomes unexercisable without its holder declining it and without any party at the holder's own table deciding about it, named with the condition lost (a permission, a capability, a counterparty, a coordination), the carrier that runs the clock, and the last intervention that could have kept it, and sorted by what the clock is made of, from clocks the holder never started to clocks the holder's own care for the option started: a closure that must strike before it can be known, a date on someone else's docket, a date on the option's parent, the holder's own development, the record's last witness, the world healing faster than the forum, a ratifier's term, a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle, a coordination's half-life, the holder's own growth, then the act that vests, the exercise that keeps, the readiness that spoils, the move on a neighbouring matter, the new state's first act, the machine that holds the option open, and the pause paper whose renewal belongs to the adversary.
map_register: Operator-grade and concrete: bank holidays and Sunday decrees, bar dates and opt-out postcards, emergency authorizations, eye patches, last-known-well times, mootness and class certification, adjournment sine die, memoranda of lease, reorganizations that absorb a vacancy, sixty-day signatures, approval ceilings, poured footings, empty flights and irrigated fields, thawed vials, first responsive pleadings, first writes, ECMO circuits and mine pumps, tolling agreements; drawn from capital controls, bankruptcy, public-health law, paediatrics, stroke care, constitutional litigation, legislatures, real property, employment, recall elections, mergers, land use, aviation and water law, cold-chain logistics, patent and civil procedure, software migration, transplant medicine, and litigation practice.

items.out: Weekend closure. The holder who waits for the notice is waiting for the one thing the closure is built never to give, and the Monday he gets is the Monday he ordered. The authority shuts the exit in the hours the holder cannot act, on the Friday night, on the bank holiday, after the Sunday address, because a closure announced is a closure defeated: the announcement is the signal to run, so the only closure that works is the one nobody was told about. Greece, the banks that did not open on Monday 29 June 2015 after a Sunday speech; Cyprus, March 2013, a bank holiday stretched past parliament's refusal of the first levy until the bail-in was law; Argentina, the corralito announced on a Saturday in December 2001; the export licence suspended and the delisting printed once it is done. What is lost is a permission, the leave to move what is yours. The clock is the authority's calendar, laid with some care over the hours you are locked out. The one move that would have kept it was a transfer on rumour, at rumour's price: being wrong, and the discount the rumour market charges; the deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing better, and the depositors who held out for a better reason than rumour received their better reason on the Monday, in the form of a closed door. So of every expiry on this map this is the one whose notice cannot precede it, and 'I will move when they announce it' is not a plan, it is a description of how the mechanism eats the person saying it. Runway-illusions' Cash behind glass counts the deposit taken into receivership on a Friday as owned and unreachable; this is the item that chose the Friday. It is not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse the founder can test by letting it pass, since a closure you can probe is not one that has to be a surprise. And it is not a withdrawn offer or a rival's foreclosure, which somebody at your own table decides: the decree is an authority's rule on a class, and nobody at your table was asked about you. The item stands on that fence and not on anything as soft as 'the exit died as a side effect': the decree names the exit and forbids it.

Bar date in the newspaper. The creditor who expects a letter has been sent one; it ran in the county paper, between the auction notices, and the law is satisfied that he read it. The claim expires on a date fixed in a proceeding he is not attending, and the rule of constructive notice deems him to know it: the bankruptcy court's bar date for proofs of claim, noticed to unknown creditors by publication; the class settlement whose opt-out date arrives on a postcard dressed as advertising, which went out with the advertising; the probate creditor's window that opens and shuts in the legal-notices column. What is lost is a permission, the standing to be paid or to sue in his own name. The clock is the bar-date order together with the fiction that publication is knowledge for anyone the debtor could not name. What would have kept it is a one-page proof of claim or a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing in the law and the one least often made, and it is least often made not from sloth but by construction: the holder who needed to file is precisely the one who was not told, so the cheapness of the cure is a courtesy extended to the people who cannot use it. Runway-illusions' Stamp's clock is a permission with a date the holder can read on the stamp; this is the date written on someone else's docket and imputed to him. It is not deal-deaths' Missing witness. Nothing is missing from the record; the record is complete. What is missing is the holder from the room.

Emergency over. The option was issued under a parent instrument with a term of its own, and it dies when the parent dies, whatever its merits and with no date printed anywhere on it. The holder who read his grant carefully and found no expiry has read the wrong paper, carefully. The emergency-use authorization ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing; the cross-state telehealth licence lapsed state by state with each state's emergency in 2021 and 2022; the wartime power, the pilot programme run under a waiver, the sub-lease that dies with the head lease. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the parent instrument's date, which the holder never signed and, having been handed a grant with no date on it, never had a reason to read, and the first task is not to check the date but to find which parent paper carries it, a task most holders discover exists on the morning after. What would have kept it is conversion, a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in one's own name, filed while the parent still stands; and conversion is slow enough that it must be begun while the emergency looks endless, which is the exact week in which beginning it looks like paranoia, so it is begun by nobody, and the endlessness is granted its full weight right up to the day it ends. It is not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date is on a docket and imputed: here the date is on a different paper than the option, and it is honest. It is not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes: this rule does not wait. It ends.

Patch before seven. The plan that waits for the child to complain about the eye is waiting for a report from the one witness who does not know there is anything to report, and it earns exactly what such a plan earns. The option expires by the holder's own development, on a schedule the holder cannot know, so the last intervention is necessarily in another hand. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years and responds less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens; the clubfoot cast in infancy; the second language spoken without an accent, which is contested as a hard window; the duckling that imprints in its first day. What is lost is a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire. The clock is the developmental timetable, and the holder is a child who does not know there is an eye to save. What would have kept it is a screening, the preschool vision check, the parent who notices a squint, so the option belongs to one person and its preservation to another; and where there is no screening programme the option expires unseen at a rate that is a property of the programme and not of the child, which is to say a property of the adults who priced the programme and passed, and the rate is theirs to keep. Last known well has a witness dating the option; this is the case where the holder cannot be its own witness at all. It is not a use-it-or-lose-it. Nothing the child does or leaves undone runs the clock, and whoever says the child should have used the eye more has confused the patient with the programme.

Last known well. The protocol dates the option by the last witness to the fact and not by the fact, so the option expires when the proof runs out while the body might still allow it, and the patient pays for a gap in somebody else's attention. The stroke patient who wakes with the deficit is ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window counts from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke lost the drug whatever hour the artery closed; the same rule condemns the opened vial with no time on the label and the sample whose chain of custody has a gap, both treated as expired at the earliest hour they could have been. What is lost is a capability, a treatment the protocol now forbids. The clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue, and give the rule its due, it asks for the one thing a chart can hold. What would have kept it is a witness, someone awake, a time written on the vial in the thirty seconds that takes, or a witness of another kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 returned the drug to patients with no witnessed onset; and the unit that owned the scanner and went on asking the chart has earned the outcomes it kept. Witness-architectures asks what must exist for a trace to form; this is the option that dies for want of a trace while the fact would still allow it. It is not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run. Here the body's clock may not have run at all. The record's has.

Mooted. The lawyer who answers a forum's slowness by moving faster has misread which of the two clocks he owns, and the ruling he gets is the one he filed for: none. The option to a decision expires because the situation resolves itself before the forum that would decide it moves, so nobody declines and nobody rules. DeFunis, 1974, the student whose challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate; the pregnancy over before the appeal; the election held before the ballot-access case; the tenant evicted before the housing court sits; the employee whose grievance is mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What is lost is a permission, the justiciability of the claim. The clock is the ratio of the forum's pace to the harm's duration, a number set by no party at the table, which is why leaning on it produces nothing but leaned-on paper. What would have kept it is a structure that outlives the individual harm: the class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which Sosna, 1975, allowed, or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, which is what Roe rested on; so the option is kept by a coordination or by a rule and never, in any case on the record, by hurrying, and the motion to expedite gets exactly the reading it earned. It is not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where the surplus is eaten along a curve: nothing here is eaten, the harm is simply over. It is not Bar date in the newspaper: there is no date anywhere, which is the thing the hurrying lawyer keeps looking for.

Session ends. The yes given in the corridor and never minuted is worth exactly the corridor, and the holder who booked it as an approval has been paid in the currency he accepted. The body that could have said yes reaches the end of its own term with the matter pending, and its successor never has to say no. The bills that die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from the beginning; the treaty signed and awaiting a parliament that is dissolved; the permit application before a council that is re-elected; the approval the old board agreed in the corridor and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting; the offer approved by a committee disbanded in the reorganization. What expires is the matter's place in the process, since the successor body starts it at zero. What is lost is a counterparty, the specific body whose yes was available. The clock is the ratifier's own calendar, election, session, or term. What would have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the corridor; none of it is expensive and all of it requires believing the body will end, which the body's own members are the last to believe. The treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone; the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no, and the sponsor who calls that a defeat flatters his bill with an enemy it never had. Deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal has a ratifier that wanted a different bargain; this is the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. It is not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by transfer. Here it is replaced by the calendar.

Landlord changes. The tenant who did not ask the friendly landlord to put the renewal on the title, because asking would have been awkward, traded the building for the absence of one awkward afternoon, and the rate was posted in advance. An option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers expires at the counterparty's next transfer, which the holder does not control and often does not see. The renewal promised by the landlord who sells to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises; the 'we'll take you back' from a manager who leaves; the side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager has never seen; the supplier's verbal priority that walks out with the account executive. What is lost is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option. The clock is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, on which the option was never written, so the successor takes free of it, and takes free of it honestly: the successor owes nothing to a promise he was never shown, and the holder who expects him to honour it is asking a stranger to pay for a friendship. What would have kept it is recording, a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors, at the cost of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement, an awkwardness that is the entire price and is, held up to the building, small. Term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair has the replacement exercising a term the friend would not have; this is the mirror, the replacement declining to honour a term the friend gave. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

Chair grown over. The person who took leave with no return date, trusting that the seat would be kept because everyone liked her, was right about being liked and wrong about what liking does to a headcount at the next planning cycle, which is nothing. The option to return rests on a vacancy the counterparty has not yet re-planned, so it expires at the counterparty's next planning cycle without anyone declining the return. The leave with no return date whose post is redistributed among three people at the next reorganization; the budget line reallocated at year end; the supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed; the co-founder's seat that the remaining founders stop leaving empty at the next hire. What expires is the return to the seat, since employment there afterwards is a new negotiation from the outside. What is lost is a capability on the counterparty's side, the shape that could receive the holder. The clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, which sets the expiry with no reference to the holder at all, and the holder who feels slighted has mistaken an absence of reference for a reference. What would have kept it is a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle must respect, or the return itself before the cycle turns; each is a line on a form, and the form went unfilled because filling it felt like distrust, which is the compliment the holder paid herself with the seat. Traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant has preparation for a future breeding its own opponents; this is the case in which no one opposes the return and the absence is simply absorbed. It is not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way. This road has closed.

Petition that goes stale. The organizer who counts the signatures gathered and not the signatures still valid is counting money in a currency that inflates by the day, and the count he brings to the clerk is the count the clerk throws out. An option that requires many simultaneous yeses expires unless the gathering outruns the decay of each yes, so a coordination has a half-life. The recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are void under Michigan's rule, or must all fall within California's hundred and sixty days; the tender offer's minimum condition that must be met by the offer's expiry; the crowd in the square that goes home; the reunion that becomes impossible one death at a time. What is lost is a coordination. The clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention, and the attention is the shorter of the two. What would have kept it is a gathering rate, paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that binds the early yeses until the last arrives; the drive that would not pay circulators on principle paid them anyway, in signatures, at a worse rate. The recall and tender cases are observed and the crowd is analogy. Who-can-be-bound's Place in line is an ordering lost by leaving; this is the coordination lost by others' leaving. It is not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter. Here many small calendars do, and no one of them can be blamed, which is the only comfort on offer.

Outgrown the buyer. The founder who raised the round because a bigger number is a better number has priced himself past the only three people who could ever have paid it, and the advice that took him there earns what advice that never looked at the buyer's balance sheet earns. The holder's own growth moves the counterparty out of reach, so the option to sell to the natural acquirer expires at the round that prices the company above what the acquirer can pay at all: a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table declining. The company whose preference stack now exceeds the largest deal its three strategic buyers have ever done; the player whose wage outgrows every club in the league but two; the practice too large for any partner to buy in and too small to be listed. What is lost is a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option. The clock is the acquirer's capacity, readable in its market value and its deal history by anyone who bothered, set against the holder's own price, which each round raises. What would have kept it is the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make, and the advisers have their reasons, none of which are the founder's. Analytical, since every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so the item stands as a mechanism and not a count, and one should not pretend to a count. Market-deaths' Slowed past the rot has a market thinning from the outside; this is the market for the holder that the holder thins by growing. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans. Here the counterparty is unchanged and the holder has left its range.

Pour the foundation. The developer who answered the council's agenda with a lawyer's letter has a letter, and the council has a new ordinance, and only one of those is a building. A permission is about to be withdrawn by a third party's rule change, and it can be kept only by an act in the world that no paper substitutes for. The building that may proceed under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes; the footings poured the week of the council vote; the nonconforming use that survives the new code only if it is in use on the effective date; the grandfathered rate kept only by the account that was open. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, Washington among them, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction, and the holder who knows which has a different week from the holder who assumed, who has the week he assumed. What would have kept it is the hole in the ground before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made, so the option can be preserved only by starting to use it, and the plan that saved the concrete for after the vote saved exactly the concrete. First-mover-forecloses holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose; this is the rule that changes for reasons of its own. It is not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right. Here one beginning vests it for good.

Slot flown empty. The regulator who wrote a use-it-or-lose-it rule and then expressed surprise at empty aircraft has been shown his rule in the sky, and may study it there. The permission expires by disuse and is kept only by exercise, so the clock runs while the holder does nothing and stops when the holder acts, and the preserving act is the exercise emptied of its purpose. The airport slot that must be flown eighty percent of the season or returned, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived; the water right under prior appropriation forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them; the trade mark abandoned after three years' non-use; the mining claim kept by annual labour; the department budget spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the regulator's usage ledger. What would have kept it is the empty flight, which costs the whole price of using the option and returns nothing but the option, so keeping and using become the same act and the option's upkeep is its exercise price, and the holder who calls that a waste is correct and has been offered no third choice. Runway-illusions' Stamp's clock has a licence that lapses without hours logged and no cash that extends it; this is the price at which it can be extended after all, hours flown for nobody. Tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry has a gate that must spend its stamp; this is the permission-holder who must burn the permission to keep it. Power-trades' Leased strike has disuse making a power unbelieved; this is disuse forfeiting it by rule. It is not Pour the foundation, one act that vests. Here no act ever finishes the keeping.

Thawed to be ready. The clinic that thawed the whole tray to be sure of serving whoever came bought its certainty with the doses it will pour out at closing, and the certainty was, on the arithmetic, the dearer of the two things it could have bought. Preparing to exercise the option starts a decay the unprepared state did not have, so the option to wait expires because the option to act was made ready. The vaccine vial that keeps for months frozen, weeks once thawed, hours once punctured; the epoxy whose pot life begins at mixing; the drawn dose; the armed fuze; the reagent brought to room temperature; the opened surgical field; the reserve army that cannot be held at the frontier through the harvest it was drawn from. What is lost is a capability, the good itself spoiling in its ready state. The clock is a chemistry, or a season, that begins at preparation and at nothing else. What would have kept it is not preparing, or preparing in the smallest unit, the single-dose vial, the small mix, the tranche thawed for the day's bookings; the objection that small units are fiddly is granted its full weight, which is the weight of a fiddle against a tray. This is the mirror of Slot flown empty, where the option dies of not being touched. Here it dies of being touched, and a holder who holds both must burn the one and refrain from readying the other, and the manager who applied one rule to both has the outcome one rule buys. It is not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a finished copy waiting, since the understudy does not spoil for having been rehearsed. It is not Kept on the machine, where the harm falls on the holder and is billed by the day. Here it falls on the good.

First or never. The inventor who gave the conference talk on Monday and called the patent attorney on Tuesday has a very well-attended talk, and in Europe that is all he has. The option must be taken before any other move on a linked matter, so its clock is the holder's own next act rather than a date, and a holder who does nothing keeps it while a holder who does anything adjacent loses it. The objection to the court's jurisdiction over the defendant, waived if left out of the first response; the patent dead in Europe on the morning of the conference talk and a year later in the United States; the appeal waived by accepting the settlement; the election of remedies; the defect in the goods that must be objected to before the goods are used; the 'speak now' at the wedding. What is lost is a permission. The clock is a rule that binds the option to a position in a sequence, and the sequence is written somewhere other than the option, in the rules of procedure, the patent statute, the sales code, so the holder learns the order from the loss, which is the one tuition the rule offers and the one it always collects. What would have kept it is the ordering itself: the provisional application filed the morning of the talk, the reservation written into the first filing, the objection lodged before the goods are unpacked, each costing nothing but the knowledge that an order exists; and the holder who had that knowledge and answered on the merits first because the merits were strong has been shown what merits are worth out of turn. It is not Slot flown empty, where the holder's inaction runs the clock. Here inaction is the only thing that keeps it. It is not Bar date in the newspaper: there is no date, and the holder is the only one who can strike, and did.

Rollback horizon. The engineer who said 'we can always roll back' was right for the length of the pause between the cutover and the new service's first write, and the sentence was still in the air when the pause ended. The option to reverse a move expires at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, so the window is the gap between the change and its first consequence, and it closes without anyone deciding to close it. The migration that can be rolled back until the new service writes its first record in a shape the old schema rejects; the merger reversible until the first combined payroll; the new address reversible until the first piece of mail arrives there; the reorganization reversible until the first hire is made into the new chart; the currency changeover until the first contract is written in the new unit. What is lost is a capability, the old state's ability to take over from here. The clock is the first write, performed by the new state in the ordinary course and not as a decision about the reversal at all, so the team that booked a go/no-go meeting for Friday booked it for a window the Tuesday batch job had already closed. What would have kept it is the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth, a price the team declined as overhead and then paid in full as a rewrite. Pivot-invariants names the retained assets that make leaving cheap; this is the moment one of them is lost. Undo-costs bills a reversal that remains possible; this is the reversal that stops being possible, and no bill is issued. It is not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good. Here the new state's use closes the way back to the old.

Kept on the machine. The board that read the bridge as time bought and spent it on nothing has been billed for the time at the bridge's rate, which was never the situation's rate. The option is held open by a device or an upkeep whose own running accumulates a harm or whose lapse is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. The patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant who becomes ineligible for the transplant the machine was keeping her alive for, since bleeding, infection, and clotting rise with each week on circuit and centres set a duration beyond which candidacy is reviewed; the mothballed mine kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening; the ship in the reserve fleet whose hull is kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end; the interim chief who has run the company past the point where the search can bring in an outsider. What is lost is a capability, the eligibility or the workings. The clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. What would have kept it is a listing at the moment of cannulation, a search begun the day the interim was named, a decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible, each of which treats the bridge's start as the option's deadline, and each of which was postponed on the ground that the bridge was holding, the one fact about a bridge that says nothing about the deadline. The ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified, and one should claim no more precision than the centres have. Lead-time-floors' Bridge is a degraded replacement priced by the hour; this is the bridge that ends the option it holds open. It is not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs. Here the clock is a harm nobody signs, and nobody was asked to.

Standstill with a term. The plaintiff who signed a tolling agreement to spare himself the cost of filing has stopped a clock he could have stopped alone, by filing, and in exchange handed the adversary a twelve-month renewal to sell him at a price the adversary now knows he will pay. A pause taken to keep an option open is written on a paper with a date, so a situation that had no deadline acquires one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the counterparty, who now knows what the pause is worth to the holder. The tolling agreement that stops the limitations clock and expires in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence that dates a job which had no date and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement that holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough whose recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover that keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What is lost is a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. The clock is the pause's own instrument, and it is the only clock in the situation that the holder wrote, which is the whole indictment: the one deadline in the room is the one he drafted. What would have kept it is the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted; the Korean armistice is the exception with no renewal date, and is still called temporary. The statutory pauses, the twelve weeks of the family-leave statute and the restraining order's fourteen days, are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Impasse-inventions' cooling-off right offers reversibility as a chip; this is the bill the chip carries. It is not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search. Here the search is stopped, and the stopping is what expires.
